stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.title: Stair Treads Lakewood Ranch FL | Builder Stairs to Wood
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.description: Converting carpeted builder stairs to LVP or hardwood treads in Lakewood Ranch, FL, matched to your main floor. HOA approval notes and 2026 pricing.
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.h1: Stair Treads in Lakewood Ranch: Builder Carpet to Wood
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.lede: Nearly every Lakewood Ranch village built the same two-story plan, and nearly every one of those staircases still hides its original builder carpet.
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.capsule: Lakewood Ranch's stair-tread work follows the community's two-story builder formula: carpeted stairs from Summerfield to Star Farms getting converted to LVP or engineered hardwood treads that match the main floor. A typical fourteen-tread LVP conversion runs $1,260-$2,380 installed in 2026; HOA design review applies before work starts.
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.body_html:
Every Lakewood Ranch village north of the original Country Club East build-out uses the same two-story floor plan formula: primary suite and main living down, secondary bedrooms up, and a staircase that came from the builder in wall-to-wall carpet over unfinished pine treads. That's true whether the house is a 2007 model in Summerfield or a 2023 close in Star Farms, and it's the single biggest stair-tread pattern in the community; see our Lakewood Ranch area page for the full village list. A two-story 2014 model in Polo Run or Mallory Park would typically carry thirteen to fifteen treads for its run, and virtually none of them still have the original builder carpet in place, since most families replace it within the first few years once the wear pattern shows in the center of each step.

We match tread material to whatever the homeowner chose for the main floor, which in Lakewood Ranch usually means engineered hardwood for the Country Club East and Lake Club crowd replacing their original 2006-era flooring, or LVP for the newer family villages that already run SPC vinyl plank through the downstairs living space. Risers get painted or stained to match, and open-tread conversions come up occasionally in the newest Star Farms and Windward phases where a homeowner wants a more modern stairwell than the builder's closed-riser default.

HOA design review applies to stair-tread work the same way it applies to any visible flooring change, even though the staircase itself sits entirely inside the house. Most villages want the material and finish submitted before work starts, which is a faster approval than a full floor replacement since it's a smaller visible change. Every tread gets custom-fabricated in our shop rather than ordered off a rack, because builder-grade stringers from different phases of construction aren't perfectly consistent even within the same village. The crew works the run one step at a time, covering a finished pair before moving up, which keeps the staircase usable for a family still living in the house through the job.
stair-treads/lakewood-ranch.cost_html:
A typical Polo Run or Mallory Park two-story model with fourteen treads, converting from carpet to LVP stair treads that match a downstairs SPC vinyl plank floor, runs $65-$105 per tread ($910-$1,470) plus risers at $25-$65 each ($350-$910), for a typical 2026 installed range of $1,260-$2,380.

A Country Club East owner upgrading the same fourteen-tread run to engineered hardwood, matching a new wide-plank main floor, runs $110-$180 per tread ($1,540-$2,520) plus the same riser range, totaling $1,890-$3,430. See our stair tread cost guide for solid hardwood and laminate tread pricing as well.

faqs.q: How many treads does a typical Lakewood Ranch two-story home have?
faqs.a: A standard two-story model in villages like Polo Run or Mallory Park typically carries thirteen to fifteen treads for its stair run, which is the range we price against for most full-staircase conversions in the community.

faqs.q: Does my Lakewood Ranch HOA need to approve new stair treads?
faqs.a: Most village design review boards want the tread material and finish submitted before work starts, the same as any visible flooring change, though approval for a staircase is usually faster than for a full floor replacement.

faqs.q: Should stair treads match my main floor in Lakewood Ranch?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's the standard we build to. Country Club East owners upgrading to engineered hardwood downstairs typically match their treads to it, while the newer family villages running SPC vinyl plank usually choose matching LVP treads instead.
